verifications.claim: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The first crewed test flight under NASA’s Artemis program'; R5: 'the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R2: 'the first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Artemis II as the first crewed Artemis mission and first beyond LEO since Apollo 17 (1972), over 50 years before 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II took four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the Moon and safely back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day journey around the Moon... safe splashdown'; R4: '10-day mission... splashing down'; R5: 'Crewed lunar flyby... 9 days, 1 hour'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm four astronauts, ~10-day duration, lunar flyby trajectory, and successful safe return via splashdown.

verifications.claim: Artemis II splashed down on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down... on Friday, April 10'; R5: 'Landing date April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)'; R2/R8: 'April 10'
verifications.reasoning: All sources agree on April 10 local/PDT time (UTC April 11), matching the claim's date.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew tested the Orion spacecraft's systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test how the spacecraft’s systems operate in a deep space environment'; R4: 'tested NASA’s Orion spacecraft during a crewed mission in deep space'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm testing Orion systems in deep space.

verifications.claim: NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen flew around the Moon, reaching the far side.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA... Jeremy Hansen'; R5: 'flew around the Moon... far side'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew named across sources; mission involved lunar flyby reaching far side.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew set a new record for the farthest distance traveled from Earth by humans, reaching 252,756 miles (406,771 km) on April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '252,756 miles from Earth'; R5: '252,756 miles (406,771 km)' on April 6; R1: '252,760 miles... surpass... Apollo 13'
verifications.reasoning: Exact distance and date match R2/R5; R1 minor rounding difference (760 vs 756); record explicitly stated.

verifications.claim: Victor Glover became the first person of color to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mr. Glover was the first Black man to travel into deep space'; R5: 'Victor Glover became the first person of color'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly attribute this milestone to Glover.

verifications.claim: Christina Koch became the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Ms. Koch the first woman'; R5: 'Christina Koch the first woman'

verifications.claim: Jeremy Hansen became the first non-U.S. citizen to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mr. Hansen the first Canadian'; R5: 'Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts performed manual flying tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'conduct manual spacecraft operations'; R4: 'practicing manual flying'; R5: 'manual control of the spacecraft'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts evaluated life support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'evaluate Orion’s life-support'; R4: 'life‑support'; R5: 'test essential life support systems'
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of evaluating/testing life support.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts tested the spacecraft's communication systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'communications at lunar distances'; R5: 'communications... tested... optical communications'
verifications.reasoning: Planned and executed tests of comms at lunar distances; O2O system tested.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II astronauts tested the new, improved toilet system.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'issue with the built-in space toilet'; R9: 'tested out the very first toilet to go to the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm testing new toilet (first to Moon), but note issues; 'improved' not directly supported.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew observed the Moon’s surface, taking photos and notes to help determine geological composition.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lunar surface observations... color, texture... geological composition'; R2: 'studied... lunar far side... observations'; R5: 'geological observations... photographed'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit lunar observations, photos, notes for geology/science.

verifications.claim: Artemis II concluded with a successful splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California after a high-speed, high-temperature reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown... Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego... high-temperature reentry'; R2/R4/R8: 'off California’s coast... high-speed'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm successful Pacific/California splashdown post high-speed/temp reentry.
